data.title: Conversion Funnel
data.tagline: A sequence of user counts and conversion rates that locates drop-off from entry to a target outcome
data.learningOutcome: You can verify funnel steps, user scope, time window, and event definitions, then read step conversion and distinguish a funnel from a user flow.
data.description: Out of 1,000 visitors, 620 may start sign-up, 310 submit details, and 280 finish. A funnel shows how many remain at each step. Mismatched event definitions, time windows, or user scopes can make the shape misleading.

learning.assumes: You can map task steps but do not yet know how behavior data locates the largest loss.
learning.outcome: You can verify funnel steps, user scope, time window, and event definitions, then read step conversion and distinguish a funnel from a user flow.

explanation.title: Define steps and the success outcome
explanation.text: Each step needs a real trackable action and an order that matches the question.

explanation.title: Use one user and time definition
explanation.text: Deduplication, entry rules, and observation windows change the result and must remain consistent.

explanation.title: Location is not cause
explanation.text: A funnel shows where to investigate; interface, rule, technical, and motivation causes still need evidence.

data.boundary: A User Flow describes the allowed path. A Conversion Funnel counts how many people actually reach each step. A flow can define funnel steps but cannot replace data.

lessonPractice.title: A sign-up funnel shows 1,000 visits, 620 starts, 310 profile submissions, and 280 completions. What should the team investigate first?

options.label: Investigate start → profile submission first, while verifying that both events use matching definitions and tracking
options.feedback: Correct. This step falls from 620 to 310, a 50% step conversion and the largest loss. Verify the data before investigating interface, rules, and user reasons.

options.label: Look only at the 280 completions and ignore intermediate steps
options.feedback: The final count cannot locate the main obstacle. Intermediate steps are the funnel's diagnostic value.

options.label: Assume the form is too long and delete fields without checking events or user feedback
options.feedback: A funnel shows where loss happens, not why. The cause still needs data checks and user evidence.

data.agentPrompt: Build a sign-up conversion funnel from this real event data: visit, start sign-up, submit profile, and complete sign-up. First verify each event definition, deduplication method, time window, and user scope. Then calculate counts, step conversion, and drop-off. Identify the largest loss, but keep possible causes as questions to validate. Do not invent user data or directly remove interface content.
